key_insight: A governed AI research system can plan, execute, and document biomedical workflows end-to-end while keeping protected data inside institutional boundaries.
clinical_relevance: This could help hospitals and research teams run more reproducible, auditable AI-assisted studies on real-world health data without exposing sensitive records.
method: Built NAIS as an agentic research system with proposal review, planning, governed compute routing, workflow orchestration, evidence tracking, and human oversight.
Tested it on a hypertension GWAS using hospital-linked genotype and EHR data from 286,422 people under an aggregate-only policy.
The system also supported a secondary drug-induced liver injury prediction workflow using a multimodal graph neural network.
evidence_signal: In the hypertension GWAS, the agent reproduced known loci including FGF5, ATP2B1, CNNM2, FTO, and GRB14, with the strongest FGF5 signal around -log10(p) ~70; the secondary DILI model achieved AUC 0.842.
watch_item: Results depend on careful human review and phenotype reconciliation, and deployment still requires strong governance, privacy controls, and reproducible oversight.
paper_title: NVAITC AI Scientist: A Governed End-to-End Research System -- A Hypertension GWAS Case Study
